note: Green circle with a green arrow SW toward Manila (the convoy's course). Measured against the printed 1-degree grid; Attack 2 is 17-13N 118-24.5E. 1300 is not the attack time (1508 I); BANG surfaced at 0710 I for an end-around and dived at 1320 I

Written beside F01: convoy HI-67 (J01). The catalog's Notoro is not this CVS: FLASHER damaged her off Borneo the same night (J02). BANG's sheet 2(b) (p27) also saw a possible CVS; sheet 2(a) (p25): at least 11 marus including two tankers and one possible CS, five or more escorts, course 225
Blue circle overlapping F01. Probably BANG's contact report after she surfaced at 0710 I. "0000/29" is written under it; meaning unclear
Written near Macclesfield Bank with a line drawn to F01. BANG fired at 1508 I
Fainter, another hand, north of 20N with a line to F01; so known at FRUPAC on 4 July. The catalog says Sarawak Maru was torpedoed by BANG

text: TA 03/1720 / 2 AK / SUNK / 1 AK / prob. / SUNK
note: Written over Luzon with an arrow to F01. BANG's claim as reported: sheets 2(a) and 2(b) (p25, p27) each claim a ship sunk, 2(c) (p29) one probably sunk. The Japanese record (J01) has two oilers with minor damage, both reaching Manila
On the dashed track into Cavite; probably the convoy's arrival at Manila Bay
Green circle; the name is hard to read. 1210 I = 1310 K, when BANG was on the surface making an end-around on the tanker (surfaced 1140 K, dived 1549 K). Measured against the bold 20N and 140E lines

Blue and green circles just south of 20N. Four hours before BANG's 0506 I attack and about 50 nm east of it; BANG had SEAHORSE's contact report at 2250 I on the 3rd, so probably SEAHORSE's attack. A note beside it reads "#28 KYODO"
Blue circle. BANG dived for a plane at 1229 I at 20-15N 115-45E (Air 33), seven minutes earlier; same longitude, latitude 0.3 degree off
